subject: Data sovereignty cutover & field sanitization blueprint — Q&A
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Hart <dr_emily_hart@medicore.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on cutover + sanitization approach for PHI

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we scope our production cutover we need a clear, auditable approach to retention and redaction for PHI. A few quick questions so we can finalize our procurement request: 

- Can Redwood enforce an EU-only storage residency for the raw transcripts + embeddings (no cross-region replication)?
- Do you support selective deletion by patient_id such that all LLM-derived artifacts (tokens, embeddings, caches) are removed within a defined SLA?
- For redaction: is field-level canonicalization (replace SSN/email fields with tokens) supported at ingestion, or do you recommend post-ingest pipeline redaction?
- What audit evidence (logs, hashes, deletion receipts) will we receive for compliance review?

We have an internal timeline: pilot in June, production cutover by Aug 1. Can you outline operational constraints or blockers?

Appreciate a concise runbook we can attach to our security review.

Best,
Emily
Dr. Emily Hart
Head of Data Governance, Medicore Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Emily Hart <dr_emily_hart@medicore.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on cutover + sanitization approach for PHI

Hi Emily — thanks for the excellent list. Below is a concise runbook addressing each question; I've attached a redaction spec and a candidate cutover timeline for your review (redaction_spec_v1.xlsx, mc_sov_cutover_timeline.pdf).

1) Residency: Yes — we can enforce EU-only storage for all persisted artifacts (raw transcripts, embeddings, fine-tuned snapshots). That is implemented at the tenant level: data-at-rest keys, object storage endpoints, and model routing are bound to an EU region. No cross-region replication will be enabled for that tenant unless you explicitly opt in.

2) Selective deletion by patient_id: Supported. Two options: 
  - Logical purge: tag all artifacts with the patient_id at ingest and run a tenant-scoped purge that deletes object store files, database rows, and invalidates/clears related KV cache entries. Targets: transcripts, prompts, response logs, embeddings.
  - Cryptographic time-bounded keys (advanced): store encrypted blobs using patient-scoped envelope keys so a key destruction renders data unrecoverable. This is recommended for stricter jurisdictions but requires changes to key rotation and backup policies.

SLA: standard deletion job completes within 48 hours for datasets under 500k objects. For larger datasets we provide streaming purge with progress and final deletion receipt. We’ll include a deletion_manifest (list of object identifiers + SHA256) as audit evidence.

3) Redaction at ingestion vs post-ingest: we recommend a hybrid approach: 
  - Ingest-time field canonicalization for structured PHI (SSN, DOB, email) using our redaction middleware. This prevents PHI from being indexed into embeddings.
  - Post-ingest scrub for free-text NER misses: periodic redaction passes with differential rules (regex + ML NER) and an approval queue for edge cases.

4) Audit evidence: you will receive
  - Deletion manifest with object IDs, timestamps, and SHA256s
  - API audit logs showing user/service initiating deletion, job ids, and status
  - Optional attestations (signed timestamps) for key destruction events if you choose the cryptographic option

Operational constraints / blockers: 
  - Embeddings: if embeddings were already materialized and distributed to search clusters, re-embedding after redaction is required to remove residual signal. That can extend the purge window.
  - KV/prefix caches: in-memory caches on inference nodes will be invalidated; however, any downstream customer-side caches (internal search indices) need their purge process coordinated.
  - SLA exceptions: very large historical stores (>10M objects) will need a staged purge and can exceed the 48-hour window.

Next steps I propose:
  1. We review and sign the cutover timeline (attached).
  2. You provide the patient_id list and any special tokenization rules.
  3. We schedule a technical run-through with Karthik to confirm embedding purge mechanics and with our Security team for artifact attestation.

I’m looping Karthik to answer the embedding and cache specifics below.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Emily Hart <dr_emily_hart@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on cutover + sanitization approach for PHI

Emily — quick technical notes (embedding/cache focused):

- If embeddings were materialized prior to redaction, we will: 
  1) mark embeddings tied to patient_id via metadata and schedule a re-embed job after the redaction pass;
  2) purge prior vectors from vector index (we support idempotent delete-by-id for all major vector stores we manage);
  3) disable hot prefixes for the affected keys to avoid serving stale results during re-indexing.

- Cache invalidation: we push an invalidation message over the cluster bus; nodes will asynchronously evict KV and prefix caches. For guaranteed freshness during a purge window we can put affected routes into a degraded mode (no batching, bypass cache) for a configurable window.

- Tokenization & canonicalization: our ingest pipeline supports field-level canonicalization via configurable redaction templates. For emails/SSNs we replace with stable tokens (e.g., [EMAIL_38b2]) so referential integrity is preserved for application purposes while PHI is removed. For legal erasure we recommend full removal (not just tokenization) unless your retention policy requires pseudonymization.

- Evidence: the deletion_manifest includes vector IDs and the vector store shard locations; we also include a re-index job id that can be cross-referenced with the audit logs.

Two quick clarifications needed from your side:
  - Will re-embedding be in-place (same model/profile) or do you want to switch to a quantized/cheaper embedding variant at re-index time?
  - Do you require deletion receipts to be cryptographically signed by an HSM-backed key? We can offer that as an optional add-on.

Happy to do a short runbook session tomorrow.

—
Karthik Iyer
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Emily Hart <dr_emily_hart@medicore.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on cutover + sanitization approach for PHI

Thanks — quick summary and actions so the security review team has what they need: 

Summary: Redwood can support EU-only residency, selective deletion by patient_id with a documented SLA (48h for small-to-medium sets), and hybrid redaction (ingest + post-ingest). Embeddings must be re-materialized to fully remove signal; we provide manifests and signed attestations as evidence.

Action items (owner / ETA):
  - Medicore: share patient_id list + any special token rules (Emily) — ETA: 2028-05-09
  - Redwood (Karthik): confirm re-embed model choice and whether signed HSM receipts required — ETA: 2028-05-06
  - Redwood (Vanessa): finalize and return the cutover timeline and the SOW addendum for data residency — ETA: 2028-05-07 (DocuSign link will be sent)

I’ve uploaded the runbook artifacts to the shared drive (link above) and attached the redaction spec. If that all looks good, I’ll open a HubSpot deal task and book the technical run-through for Monday.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for regulated workloads
